parsed.why: No trans-specific criminal or border rule; strong constitutional/court protections. But documented police extortion and abuse of gender-nonconforming people, nightlife raids, impunity warnings, transfemicides and document-mismatch discrimination leave everyday exposure high.

State-imposed universal exposure: sex-assigned-at-birth passport/visa rules, X-marker abolition, refusals and stranding, facilities bans across many states plus documented bathroom arrest and men's-ward custody. Litigation and hate-crime law only partly offset.

Same-sex conduct criminalised (three months to two years), no recognition, police refuse to investigate anti-LGBTQ crimes, official and social hostility, no recourse. Sodomy law's police-lever use and impunity dominate a thin dossier.

No criminalisation and court-recognised self-ID, but no working document procedure, documented provincial discrimination, physical and sexual harassment, conversion therapy and rising anti-LGBT political rhetoric with death threats. Hostility with thin recourse.

No criminalisation, functioning courts, no documented trans-specific police, border or facility exposure. Main gap is hate-crime enforcement, found violated by a regional court but reopened on order; sparse scene, no trans-specific negatives documented.
